title: Quiz: The Pure Birth Process — Yule Model

questions.text: In the Yule process with individual birth rate λ, if the current population is n, what is the total instantaneous birth rate?
options: nλ (each of n individuals contributes rate λ independently)
n²λ (pairs of individuals interact to produce offspring)
questions.explanation: In the Yule model, λₙ = nλ. Each of the n individuals contributes an independent birth rate λ, so the total rate of the next birth (by any individual) is nλ. This is because the minimum of n independent Exp(λ) random variables is Exp(nλ).

questions.text: The Yule process starting from 1 individual has N(t) following a Geometric distribution with parameter p = e^{-λt}.
questions.explanation: The solution to the Yule ODE system gives P_n(t) = e^{-λt}(1-e^{-λt})^{n-1} for n=1,2,3,... This is the Geometric(p) PMF with p=e^{-λt} on the support {1,2,3,...}. As t increases, p decreases toward 0, shifting probability mass toward larger population sizes.

questions.text: What is the mean population size E[N(t)] in the Yule process starting from 1 individual?
questions.explanation: E[N(t)] = 1/p(t) = 1/e^{-λt} = e^{λt}. This is exponential growth — the expected population doubles every ln(2)/λ time units. For λ=0.3/hour, the population doubles approximately every 2.31 hours.

questions.text: In the Gillespie (kinetic Monte Carlo) algorithm for the Yule process, when the population is currently n, the waiting time until the next birth is drawn from:
questions.explanation: When n individuals are present, each gives birth at rate λ independently. The time until the first birth (among n individuals) is the minimum of n i.i.d. Exp(λ) random variables, which has distribution Exp(nλ). So the Gillespie algorithm draws the waiting time from Exp(rate = nλ).

questions.text: In the integrating factor solution for P_n(t) in the Yule ODE, the integrating factor is:
questions.explanation: The ODE is dP_n/dt + nλP_n = RHS. To solve a linear first-order ODE of the form y' + py = q, the integrating factor is e^{∫p dt} = e^{nλt}. Multiplying both sides by e^{nλt} converts the left side into d/dt[e^{nλt}P_n(t)].

questions.text: Var[N(t)] = e^{λt}(e^{λt} - 1) grows faster than E[N(t)] = e^{λt} for large t, meaning the coefficient of variation (SD/mean) grows over time.
questions.explanation: SD = sqrt(e^{λt}(e^{λt}-1)) ≈ e^{λt} for large t. CV = SD/Mean ≈ e^{λt}/e^{λt} = 1 for large t. Actually, CV → 1 (not growing), but the variance e^{2λt} grows much faster than the mean e^{λt}. The Yule process is increasingly variable in absolute terms — the standard deviation is comparable to the mean.
